Research · Side A

Models that perform well—and deserve to be trusted.

My PhD combines large-scale K–12 data, LLMs, structured representations, and systematic evaluation of explanations for reliability, fairness, and actionability.

01 / Explainable AILAK 2027 · under review
.646forward simulation

Beyond Fidelity

A verifier-constrained Qwen3-8B framework that proposes and evaluates revisions to executable early-warning explanations, separating model fidelity from an observer’s ability to apply an explanation.

  • .89fidelity
  • .646simulation
  • .846counterfactual
Qwen3-8BProxy simulatabilityHuman-centred XAI
02 / Unified modelingAISTATS 2027 · under review
14school levels

OneForAll

A DistilBERT-to-neural-classifier pipeline that unifies heterogeneous K–12 student records without manual schema alignment.

  • 2.5Mrecords
  • 79%dropout recall
  • 0.83AUC
TransformersLIMEHeterogeneous data
03 / LLMsAIED · 2024
77%recall with few-shot RAG

LLMs for dropout detection

RAG-assisted few-shot prediction with Zephyr-7B and Mistral-7B, producing student-level rationales alongside predictions.

RAGFew-shot learningRationales
04 / FairnessAIED · 2025
≠accuracy is not equity

Fairness of ensemble learning

A benchmark across 14 sub-datasets and four protected attributes showing that greater model complexity does not guarantee fairer predictions.

ABROCAEnsemblesResponsible AI
05 / Representation auditAIED · 2026
3M+records audited

When textification fails

Five encoders and five text templates reveal how long inputs collapse representations—and how “fairness through blindness” can mislead.

Embedding collapseSpectral analysisFairness
06 / Evidence synthesisJAIED · under review
XAIexplainable + fair ML

Explainable and fair ML for K–12

A systematic review of explainability and fairness in machine-learning approaches to student dropout prediction, with an emphasis on responsible human-in-the-loop support.

Systematic reviewExplainabilityFairness
